title: Starting a conversation from a page: the questions before anything is drawn

steps.path: A page's button, such as Frontier Lab's Update now
steps.headline: When you press the button, should it go straight to the new conversation or show the new-conversation window first?
steps.today: Frontier Lab's Update now shows a request in a box with a Copy button. You open a new conversation yourself and paste it.
steps.problem: That is several steps for something you do every week, and it is easy to forget or paste into the wrong place.
steps.proposal: Pressing the button would open a new conversation in the page's project with the request typed in the box. The question is whether you get a chance to adjust settings first.

options.label: Straight in
pros: One press, then Enter.
Uses your usual folder-and-model settings, so nothing new to decide.
The approval card already checked with you the first time.
cons: You cannot pick a cheaper or stronger assistant for this one run without changing it afterwards.

options.label: Show window first
pros: You see and can change the model every time.
Works as an extra confirmation.
cons: One more click every week.
Adds little safety, since the request still waits for your Enter.

steps.path: A page's button, such as Frontier Lab's Update now
steps.headline: Should the request be sent for you, or wait in the box until you press Enter?
steps.today: Today nothing is sent for you; you paste and press Enter yourself.
steps.problem: Waiting costs one key press. Sending for you saves it, but the assistant would start working before you have read anything.
steps.proposal: The proposal is that it always waits for your Enter. A per-page choice could be added later if the extra key press annoys you.

options.label: Always waits
pros: Nothing runs until you have looked at it.
A page from someone else can never act on its own.
cons: One extra key press.

options.label: Sent automatically
pros: Truly one press.
cons: The assistant starts before you read anything.
A page from someone else becomes much more risky.

options.label: Your choice per page
pros: Convenience for pages you trust, such as your own.
cons: One more checkbox to understand on the approval card.

steps.path: A page's button, such as Frontier Lab's Update now
steps.headline: Should the page be able to type its own message text, such as 'update only the Papers section'?
steps.today: The page can only show the request it was built with.
steps.problem: A page that needs variations, such as one section only, needs a separate fixed message for each.
steps.proposal: Either the page may only use fixed messages you approved, or it may write its own text each time.

options.label: Fixed messages only
pros: What you approved is exactly what gets typed.
Words from a website cannot sneak into the request.
cons: The page needs one entry per variation.

options.label: Page writes its own
pros: Flexible: any variation without extra setup.
cons: The approval card can no longer show you what will be typed.
A page that reads websites could pass their words along, even though you would still see it before pressing Enter.

steps.intro: How YouCoded makes sure a page cannot start work you did not expect.

steps.path: A page's button, such as Frontier Lab's Update now
steps.headline: If your usual setting is to skip permission questions, should a conversation started by a page skip them too?
steps.today: Your normal conversations follow your own setting about asking before risky actions.
steps.problem: A page could quietly start a conversation that runs commands without asking you.
steps.proposal: Either page-started conversations always ask first, or they follow your usual setting and the card tells you so.

options.label: Always ask
pros: A page can never start a conversation that acts without asking.
Stays safe even if you later allow sending for you.
cons: A weekly update may stop more often to ask you.

options.label: Follow my setting
pros: Same as all your other conversations.
cons: Combined with sending for you, a page could start unattended work.

steps.path: A page's button, such as Frontier Lab's Update now
steps.headline: When should the approval card appear: the first time you press the button, or before the page opens?
steps.today: Other page abilities, such as reaching websites, ask you before the page opens.
steps.problem: Asking up front would make you answer about a button you may never press.
steps.proposal: The card would appear as a window over the page the first time you press the button, naming the project and quoting the message word for word.

options.label: First press
pros: Asked exactly when it makes sense.
Frontier Lab opens normally.
cons: Differs from other abilities, which ask before the page opens.

options.label: Before page opens
pros: One familiar card with everything up front.
cons: Frontier Lab cannot be read until you answer a question about a button you may not press.

steps.path: A page's button, such as Frontier Lab's Update now
steps.headline: How many times may a page start a conversation?
steps.today: A page has no way to start conversations yet, so there is no limit to set.
steps.problem: A broken page that repeats a click could fill your screen with conversations.
steps.proposal: Proposed: one every 30 seconds and five an hour, and only when you actually press something.

options.label: 30 seconds, 5 an hour
pros: Stops runaway pages.
Plenty for a weekly button.
cons: A page with several buttons used in a burst may say 'try again shortly'.

options.label: Only on a press
pros: Simplest.
cons: A buggy page could open many conversations.

steps.path: A page's button, such as Frontier Lab's Update now
steps.headline: After each weekly Frontier Lab update, what should happen to the 'Code changed since you allowed this' note?
steps.today: YouCoded shows that note when a page's code changes after you approved it. Frontier Lab rewrites its own page every week.
steps.problem: You would see the note after every update, and a note that always appears gets ignored.
steps.proposal: Three ways to handle it, from quiet to more work.

options.label: Hide for these pages
pros: No weekly nagging.
The message is checked separately, so a changed message still asks again.
cons: You are not told when such a page's code changes.

options.label: Keep the note
pros: Consistent with other pages.
cons: You learn to ignore it.

options.label: Change Frontier Lab
pros: The note then means a real code change.
cons: Needs work in the Frontier Lab project.
The page loads its data a moment later.

steps.intro: Which pages and which devices get this ability.

steps.path: Pages that are not inside a project, such as your personal pages
steps.headline: Should your personal pages, which are not in a project, be able to start a conversation?
steps.today: Frontier Lab belongs to a project, so the new conversation would open in that project's folder. Personal pages have no such folder.
steps.problem: A personal dashboard cannot start a conversation, but giving it a folder is harder to keep predictable.
steps.proposal: Project pages only, or personal pages too with a folder chosen some way.

options.label: Project pages only
pros: The folder is always obvious and fixed.
Least to build and least to go wrong.
cons: A personal dashboard cannot start a conversation.

options.label: Use default folder
pros: Works everywhere.
cons: Your default folder can change, so conversations could land somewhere unexpected.

options.label: Ask for a folder once
pros: Flexible and explicit.
cons: More on the card to read and remember.

steps.path: Approving from your phone while it is paired to the computer
steps.headline: Should you be able to allow a page's request from your phone?
steps.today: Some approvals on the phone are sent to the computer to finish there.
steps.problem: A quick tap on a small screen is easier to do without reading the message.
steps.proposal: Either the phone approves like the computer, or it says 'Finish on your computer'.

options.label: Yes, on the phone
pros: The button works the same everywhere.
No secret is involved and the conversation opens visibly.
cons: Easier to tap without reading the message.

options.label: Computer only
pros: Approvals happen on the bigger screen.
cons: The first use must be on the computer.
